posts:
Father stops school shooting.
Evidence: 4 dead, armed bystander intervention, Silver Rail Elementary
#2A #Oregon 🌐

An armed bystander, identified as father Kaylub Giamanco, intervened during an active shooter attack at Silver Rail Elementary, stopping the gunman.
Stated Judgement: (+1.00, +1.00) — Greater Good

While Giamanco's courageous intervention halted the rampage, four innocent lives were lost, and the bystander suffers heavy survivor's guilt.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.03, -0.75) — Greater Evil

Verdict: CONDITIONAL — Fall into Destruction.
An armed citizen stopped a horrific tragedy, but four deaths and immense trauma underscore the heavy cost of violence.

Integrity: Conditionally Sound (Hypocrisy: 1.8, z: 2)

- Armed Intervention: PASS (0.9, 0.5) — Stopped active shooter instantly.
- Ideological Framing: COND (-0.2, -0.5) — Exploits tragedy for blanket gun policy advocacy.
Kaylub Giamanco, a 36-year-old father and carpenter carrying concealed, heard gunfire at Silver Rail Elementary and confronted the 16-year-old shooter.

The Bright Side:
Quick civilian intervention prevented further loss of life during an active school shooting.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing tactical intervention with systemic safety. Stopping a shooter is heroic, but treating it as a substitute for prevention is a category error.

Social Physics Analysis:
A grieving father acted with immense personal courage to save children, while media outlets immediately weaponize the bloodshed for polarized culture-war debates.

The Trajectory: The Path of Fall into Destruction.
When you map the gap between ideological narratives and the raw trauma of school shootings, it plots a trajectory toward Lesser Good. Real heroism meets deep tragedy.

The Unavoidable Truth: Armed intervention by a bystander stopped an active shooter from killing more children.

The Unavoidable Lie: Individual concealed carry is a sufficient systemic solution to school violence.

Alethekanon:
Heroism in crisis deserves profound respect, but reducing a multi-victim school shooting to a talking point for firearm policy avoids confronting systemic failure.

Awwthekanon:
My heart breaks for the families who lost children and for the father carrying such heavy grief and guilt despite doing all he could to save lives.

Brothekanon:
That dad is an absolute hero for running in there, but it's heartbreaking that kids still had to die in a school.

Spirithekanon:
"Greater love has no one than this: to lay down one's life for one's friends." John 15:13 — PASS
Stepping into mortal danger to protect the innocent reflects the highest measure of sacrificial love amid devastating tragedy.

Bystander Who Killed School Shooter Identified as Father Who Carries Concealed

The bystander who police said shot and killed the Silver Rail Elementary shooter has been identified as Kaylub Giamanco, the father of two daughters who attend the school.
The post Bystander Who Killed School Shooter Identified as Father Who Carries Concealed appeared first on Breitbart.

Actual Article Body:
The bystander who police said shot and killed the Silver Rail Elementary shooter has been identified as Kaylub Giamanco, the father of two daughters who attend the school.

Breitbart News pointed to a CBS report that law enforcement indicated the shooter “was shot and killed by a bystander.”

The New York Post identified the bystander as Giamanco, “a 36-year-old carpenter and father” who carries concealed and heard gunshots as he drove by the school during his lunchbreak.

Giamanco entered the school and cornered and killed the 16-year-old shooter in the school’s “special-education room.”

The attacker was able to kill four innocents in the attack and one of Giamanco’s siblings told the Post he “is riddled with guilt for not saving more people.”

NYC girl, 5, killed by mom suffered heart, brain injuries, DA reveals — as family reels: ‘I forgive my daughter’

Cabello walked slowly into court with her head down, wearing white overalls cuffed behind her back, remaining silent and catatonic throughout the proceeding.

Actual Article Body:
Switch between CA and NY editions here.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

The 5-year-old Queens girl battered to death by her mother suffered gruesome injuries to her heart, eyes, lungs, and brain, prosecutors revealed Friday — as the confessed killer was held without bail.

The disturbing details emerged as Francis Cabello, who chillingly told a 911 operator, “I killed my daughter,” was arraigned in Queens Criminal Court on second-degree murder charges.

First responders discovered the youngster, Fabiana Cabello, in her South Richmond Hill home just before 7 p.m. Wednesday after her 32-year-old mother made the harrowing confession.

Franklin Cabello, the grandfather of the victim, told reporters outside court in Spanish, “As a family, we feel mentally and physically destroyed. We can’t think [clearly] but we put our confidence in God.”

“She was very respectful, quiet, and she always treated me like a father, she treated me with respect… She loved her daughter… She wasn’t in control. She didn’t make this decision in her right mind. She was under some kind of influence”

“I forgive my daughter,” he said with tears in his eyes.

When officers arrived at the family’s home, they immediately began CPR on the unconscious child.

“But given the severity of her condition, they didn’t even wait for an ambulance,” Assistant District Attorney Lindsey Ruzza said, describing how police placed the girl in a patrol car and rushed her to Jamaica Hospital, where she was pronounced dead.

Ruzza explained the mom made several statements to police “in reference to not only killing the child but wanting to have killed her child.”

The young girl was allegedly in good health and running around her home for hours before her mother brought her to a second-floor bedroom, locked the door and emerged alone 45 minutes later to call 911.

Fabiana was found by first responders face down on the floor with blood coming out of her nose.

Francis and her daughter were the only two people in the room, police said.

At the time of her arrest, Francis appeared stoic and didn’t shed a tear while she was carted away in handcuffs, according to a neighbor who identified himself as Carlos.

“She was not crying, it was like nothing happened,” he told The Post.

“It’s too much emotions together. I feel sad for the child.”

Erika Santiago, 43, a licensed practical nurse who lives across the street, said she heard “a lot of yelling” Wednesday night before the emergency response.

“I heard about this when I woke up this morning at 6 o’clock and it’s absolutely devastating, devastating,” said Santiago, who has two daughters of her own, 10 and 12.

“And it’s right across the street and they brought her to the hospital I work at. It’s so close to home.”

An autopsy conducted by Dr. Lin of the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner revealed scrapes to the child’s face, petechiae in her eyes, heart and lungs, a swollen brain, bruises to her extremities, and intramuscular hemorrhaging on her shoulder blade and lower back — findings consistent with asphyxiation, according to court documents and prosecutors.

Additional reporting by Marie Pohl
